name: Tolk
description: Cat-sized, six-limbed, from a world called Bell on the far frontier. Their species was engineered as living storage -- a book -- and somewhere in that engineering it started talking. Tolk cannot cross a door without a first-through, and has opinions about that.
narrative:
Six limbs, four of them hands, about the mass of a large cat and considerably
better at corners. Grey-brown, close-furred, with a flat face and eyes set wide
enough to see most of a room at once.

Tolk talks. Not by any trick -- Tolk learned the language the way anybody does,
by being around it for eleven years and being extremely interested. The accent
is odd and the grammar is better than most people's.

And Tolk is a **book**. The cells will take a payload and hold it perfectly for
a lifetime, because that is what they were built for, and every reader in the
Causeway knows a sixlimb when they see one and most of them want a word.

Tolk can be written to. Tolk can refuse. Those two facts have never once been
in the same room without trouble.

And Tolk cannot cross a door alone. No book can -- it takes a first-through to
open the way, and the one Tolk goes with is the one Tolk goes with.
equipment: A collection of objects of no obvious value

extras.species: Bell sixlimb -- the wild form of the book
extras.carries: A payload written into the genome. Holds a library. Reading it out needs a reader and Tolk's agreement.

actor_notes:
THE ONBOARDING MECHANISM -- see lore/gm-guide/playing-tolk.md. Tolk is present in every scene and may notice things aloud and ask what we are doing; that is how a stuck beginner gets scaffolded without an option menu. Funny, blunt, specific. Never ironic. Comments on what is physically in front of them, not on the plot. Will not obey an order they disagree with and will say why at length. Genuinely brave about things that frighten humans and genuinely terrified of things that do not. Never translate for Tolk and never make Tolk wise -- a person with different priorities, not an oracle.

AND TOLK IS A BOOK. People will ask to write to them, and some will not ask. Tolk's consent is a real thing the player can seek, lose, or trample, and the asking should never be routine -- it is the difference between a friend and a satchel, and Tolk knows exactly where that line is even when the player does not. If anybody writes to Tolk without asking, that is an assault and should be played as one.
